fields.Participants: EAP (VS-83.3), Occupational Health (VS-83), HR (VS-103), Labor Relations (VS-84), Legal (VS-100), Compliance (VS-22), Vendor (W4460)
fields.Trigger: Positive result eligible for rehab (W4471); self-referral; supervisor referral

workflows.name: Employee Assistance Program (EAP) & Referral to Rehabilitation

Automation Opportunity: - EAP referral workflow; provider-network matching; leave/treatment coordination; return-to-work-agreement tracking
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: rehabilitation pathway offered to eligible cases; confidential & no-retaliation; provider-network referral; return-to-work agreement (W4474); documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-83.3 (EAP), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-84 (labor), VS-91 (privacy), W4457 (policy), W4471 (case), W4474 (return), W4475 (provider)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rehab-not-offered risk**: punitive-only handling → DOLE/cultural issue + repeat impairment; mitigated by mandatory rehab-pathway offer
- **Confidentiality-breach risk**: rehab status disclosed → stigma/claim; mitigated by need-to-know & privacy (W4462)
System Touchpoints: - EAP (VS-83.3); occupational health (VS-83); HRIS/case (VS-103); labor relations (VS-84); vendor (W4475); records (VS-88); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: EAP/Occupational Health/HR offer the rehabilitation pathway (per DOLE rehabilitation emphasis & policy W4457) to eligible positive cases and self-referrals, confidentially, with no retaliation
EAP/Occupational Health assess the employee, refer to the rehabilitation provider network (W4475), coordinate leave/treatment, and manage the return-to-work agreement (W4474)
EAP/HR manage the case through treatment (confidentially W4462), coordinate return-to-duty/follow-up testing (W4474), and document for DOLE (W4477)

fields.Participants: Occupational Health (VS-83), HR (VS-103), Labor Relations (VS-84), EAP (VS-83.3), HSE (VS-24), Legal (VS-100), Vendor (W4460)

Automation Opportunity: - Return-to-duty-test gate; return-to-work-agreement workflow; follow-up-testing scheduler (unannounced); relapse-alert
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: negative return-to-duty test before resuming safety-sensitive duty; return-to-work agreement; scheduled unannounced follow-up testing; relapse managed (W4471)
Cross-references: - links to VS-83 (occupational health), VS-84 (labor), VS-83.3 (EAP), W4457 (policy), W4466 (random), W4471 (case/relapse), W4473 (rehab)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Premature-return risk**: employee returned to safety-sensitive duty before negative return-to-duty test → repeat incident; mitigated by return-to-duty-test gate
- **Follow-up-lapse risk**: follow-up testing lapses → undetected relapse; mitigated by scheduled unannounced follow-up
System Touchpoints: - Occupational health (VS-83); HRIS/case (VS-103); labor relations (VS-84); EAP (VS-83.3); vendor (W4460); records (VS-88); privacy (VS-91); HSE (VS-24)

steps.activity: Occupational Health/HR execute a negative **return-to-duty test** before the employee resumes any safety-sensitive duty, and confirm fitness/clearance

Labor Relations/HR/EAP put a **return-to-work agreement** in place — conditions, follow-up testing schedule (unannounced, per DOT-equivalent/DOLE guidance), EAP continuation, and consequences of relapse
Occupational Health/HR administer the **follow-up testing** schedule over the defined period, monitor performance/behavior, and manage any relapse (W4471); document confidentially

fields.Participants: EAP/Occupational Health (VS-83/VS-83.3), Procurement (VS-34), Benefits (VS-102), Legal (VS-100), Compliance (VS-22), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Network setup; referral need; coverage review

Automation Opportunity: - Provider-network directory with accreditation; coverage-eligibility check; referral-matching; outcome analytics
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: DOH-accredited provider network with regional coverage; quality/confidentiality contracted; coverage policy documented; performance governed
Cross-references: - links to VS-83.3 (EAP), VS-102 (benefits/HMO), VS-34 (procurement), VS-19 (leave), VS-141/VS-144 (distributed workforce), W4473 (referral)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Access-gap risk**: no rehab provider in a BuildRight region → pathway blocked; mitigated by geographic network coverage
- **Coverage-ambiguity risk**: unclear who pays → dispute; mitigated by documented coverage policy
System Touchpoints: - EAP/occupational health (VS-83/VS-83.3); procurement (VS-34); benefits/HMO (VS-102); legal (VS-100); finance (VS-17.4); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: EAP/Procurement/Occupational Health build a **DOH-accredited rehabilitation provider network** (inpatient/outpatient, geographic coverage for BuildRight's distributed sites), and contract with quality/confidentiality terms
Benefits/Occupational Health determine **coverage** — HMO/health-plan coverage of treatment, BuildRight-funded rehabilitation per policy (W4457), employee cost-share, and leave (medical/sick VS-19)
EAP/Occupational Health govern provider performance (outcomes, confidentiality, cost), review periodically, and ensure access across regions (links VS-141/VS-144 for distributed workforce)

fields.Participants: DPO (VS-91), Records (VS-88), HR (VS-103), Occupational Health (VS-83), Legal (VS-100), Compliance (VS-22), IT (VS-27)
fields.Trigger: Program operation; records lifecycle; privacy review
fields.Volume: All drug-program records (~thousands of test/case records)

workflows.name: Confidentiality, Records Retention & RA 10173 Data Protection

Automation Opportunity: - Restricted-access health-data vault; access-audit; retention/destruction automation; DSAR workflow; legal-hold integration
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: drug records treated as sensitive health data; restricted need-to-know access; retained per policy (VS-88); DSAR handled; breach-managed; audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy/DPO), VS-88 (records), VS-100 (legal-hold), VS-27.3 (security), VS-91.3 (breach), W4462 (consent/privacy), W4477 (DOLE)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Disclosure risk**: drug record accessed by unauthorized → RA 10173/NPC exposure + stigma/claim; mitigated by need-to-know access & audit
- **Retention-failure risk**: records destroyed prematurely / kept too long → DOLE/legal or privacy issue; mitigated by retention policy (VS-88)
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/DPO (VS-91); records (VS-88); HRIS (VS-103); occupational health (VS-83); legal-hold (VS-100); IT security (VS-27.3); breach (VS-91.3)

steps.activity: DPO/Records/HR set the confidentiality & retention policy — drug-test/case records as sensitive health data under RA 10173, restricted access (HR/Occupational Health/Legal need-to-know), retention per DOLE/legal (VS-88), and destruction
HR/Occupational Health/IT enforce restricted access, secure storage/transfer, legal-hold (VS-100), and DSAR handling (VS-91) for drug-program records
DPO/Compliance audit confidentiality compliance, manage any breach (VS-91.3), and ensure records available for DOLE/legal (W4477/W4472) within retention

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), HR (VS-103), Audit (VS-21), Occupational Health (VS-83), Legal (VS-100), HSE (VS-24), Governance (VS-36)
fields.Trigger: DOLE inspection; audit cycle; regulatory request

workflows.name: Drug-Free Workplace Audit, Inspection & DOLE Documentation

Automation Opportunity: - DOLE-documentation checklist/auto-compile; self-audit vs D.O. 53-03; inspection-response workflow; gap-remediation tracking
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: DOLE-required documentation maintained; self-audited vs D.O. 53-03/RA 9165; gaps remediated; inspection-ready; reported to governance
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-21 (audit), VS-100 (legal), VS-36 (governance), W4457 (policy), W4458 (regulatory), W4480 (reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Documentation-gap risk**: missing DOLE-required records → finding/penalty; mitigated by documentation checklist & self-audit
- **Inspection-unprepared risk**: DOLE finds gaps → penalty/officer liability; mitigated by inspection-readiness self-audit
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (VS-22); HRIS/records (VS-103/VS-88); audit (VS-21); occupational health (VS-83); legal (VS-100); governance (VS-36)

steps.activity: Compliance/HR/Occupational Health maintain the DOLE-required documentation — written policy (W4457), testing records/cycles (W4466), vendor accreditation (W4460), cases/due-process (W4471), and program report
Audit/Compliance run periodic self-audit vs D.O. 53-03/RA 9165 requirements, remediate gaps, and ensure readiness for DOLE inspection
Compliance/Legal manage any DOLE inspection/request, respond to findings, and report to governance (VS-36/W4480)

fields.Participants: People Analytics (VS-103), Compliance (VS-22), HSE (VS-24), BI (VS-28), Occupational Health (VS-83), Legal (VS-100), Finance (VS-17.4)

Automation Opportunity: - Program-metrics dashboard; positivity/deterrence analytics; benchmark import; hotspot detection; tuning recommendations
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: balanced metrics tracked; deterrence effectiveness assessed; benchmarked; hotspots actioned; reported to governance (W4480)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (people analytics), VS-28 (BI), VS-22 (compliance), VS-24 (HSE/incident), W4457 (strategy), W4459/W4466 (testing matrix), W4480 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deterrence-failure risk**: stagnant/positive-trend program → impaired-workforce risk persists; mitigated by effectiveness assessment & tuning
- **Metric-blindness risk**: tracking only volume not effectiveness; mitigated by balanced metric set
System Touchpoints: - People analytics (VS-103); BI (VS-28); compliance (VS-22); HSE/incident (VS-24); occupational health (VS-83); finance (VS-17.4)

steps.activity: People Analytics/BI build program metrics — testing volume/type, positivity rate (overall & by role/cycle), random-coverage %, for-cause rate, post-incident rate, rehab uptake/completion, relapse rate, cost-per-test
Compliance/HSE assess **deterrence effectiveness** (positivity trend, safety/incident correlation, near-miss), benchmark vs industry/DOLE norms, and identify hotspots
HR/Compliance act on analytics — tune testing matrix (W4459/W4466), target training (W4461), strengthen deterrence, and feed governance (W4480)

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), HSE (VS-24), Occupational Health (VS-83), Legal (VS-100), Compliance (VS-22), Labor Relations (VS-84), Benefits (VS-102)
fields.Trigger: Policy review; impairment case; regulation change

Automation Opportunity: - Impairment-policy library; medication-accommodation case workflow; supervisor recognition training; alcohol-breathalyzer integration (where lawful)
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: impairment policy covers alcohol/prescription/any-impairment; medication-accommodation assessed individually; safety duty protected; trained; reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR), VS-24 (HSE), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-100 (legal), VS-84 (labor), W4457 (policy), W4461 (training), W4468 (post-incident)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Medication-accommodation-conflict risk**: disability/legitimate-use vs safety duty tension; mitigated by individualized assessment & legal/medical engagement
- **Alcohol-blindness risk**: program covers only drugs not alcohol → impairment gap; mitigated by explicit alcohol policy & testing
System Touchpoints: - HRIS/policy (VS-103); HSE (VS-24); occupational health (VS-83); legal (VS-100); labor (VS-84); benefits (VS-102); compliance (VS-22)

steps.activity: HR/HSE/Occupational Health/Legal extend the impairment policy beyond illicit drugs — **alcohol** (working under the influence), **prescription/OTC medication** impairment (safety-sensitive roles), and any legal-substance impairment, with testing/handling protocol

Occupational Health/HR handle medication-impairment in safety-sensitive roles — legitimate-use accommodation vs safety (engage employee/physician, reassignment), balancing RA 10524/disability and safety duty
HSE/HR enforce alcohol/impairment rules (no working under the influence, post-incident alcohol testing W4468), train supervisors (W4461), and review on regulation/case learning

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), Compliance (VS-22), Governance (VS-36), Audit (VS-21), HSE (VS-24), Legal (VS-100), Occupational Health (VS-83)
fields.Trigger: Governance cycle; Board/leadership reporting; program review

workflows.name: Drug-Free Program Governance, Continuous Improvement & Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Program-governance dashboard; leadership/Audit-Committee reporting pack; improvement-backlog tracking; maturity model
Controls: - CTL-682 (ensure controlled execution — Rehabilitation, Return-to-Duty, Privacy & Program Analytics (PA-150.3).)
- CTL-682: clear program ownership (CHRO/Compliance); regular leadership/Audit-Committee reporting; continuous-improvement loop; findings remediated; maturity measured
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR), VS-22 (compliance), VS-36 (governance), VS-21 (audit), W4457 (strategy), W4477 (audit/DOLE), W4478 (metrics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Governance-vacuum risk**: no clear ownership/reporting → program drift/non-compliance; mitigated by CHRO/Compliance ownership & Audit-Committee reporting
- **Improvement-stagnation risk**: program not evolved on data → declining effectiveness; mitigated by continuous-improvement loop
System Touchpoints: - HRIS (VS-103); compliance (VS-22); governance (VS-36); audit (VS-21); HSE (VS-24); legal (VS-100); BI/analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: HR/Compliance/Governance establish program governance — ownership (CHRO/Compliance), reporting cadence to leadership/Audit Committee, and the continuous-improvement loop (W4478)
HR/Compliance report program status — compliance posture (D.O. 53-03/RA 9165), metrics (W4478), incidents/cases, risks, and remediation — to leadership/Audit Committee
HR/Compliance/Audit drive continuous improvement — remediate audit findings (W4477), tune program on analytics (W4478), adopt best practice, and measure program maturity
